cleanup.notes: Setup (npm ci in starter/) creates starter/node_modules, which holds the pinned Vitest 4.1.12 test runner; Vitest keeps its temporary transform cache inside starter/node_modules too. Cleanup deletes starter/node_modules; the tests create nothing else and make no network requests: every fetch in the lab is a fake function supplied by the public tests. Resetting the learner's work means copying starter/api.mjs back from a fresh copy of the lab and deleting the learner-created starter/format-distance.test.mjs. The expected output file writes the lab path, start time and durations as placeholders; its 9-test total assumes the exactly-two tests Task 7 requires. Task 7 is graded by behavior: tests/your-test.test.mjs runs the learner's file through the pinned Vitest CLI with tests/your-test.vitest.config.mjs three times, against the shipped formatDistance and against two broken in-memory copies (wrong label, wrong km); it requires exactly two tests that pass on the shipped function, both failing on the wrong label and at least one failing on the wrong km. Those nested runs keep their cache inside starter/node_modules. The 45-minute cap is a planning allowance inside the 54 minutes of S26 Guided lab the intake assigns this lab, and the 38-minute median is a task-by-task authoring estimate of README reading plus the complete required task set: about 4 minutes to read the README, about 26 minutes for tasks 1 to 6 (small single functions with their contracts inline) and about 8 minutes for Task 7 (a behavior-graded two-test file whose first line the README states). The one-time setup (npm ci) is done before the block and is not counted. The Windows broken-copy path comparison in tests/your-test.vitest.config.mjs folds letter case on win32 but has no recorded Windows run; Windows support for Task 7 is unverified. Every task is required; there are no stretch tasks. Neither number is a measured learner pilot.
